newsitem.title: CHINA: China shares indices end down on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: China shares indices end down on cautious mood.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended down on Friday, with most investors more cautious on news of plans to further tighten controls on the financial markets, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index fell 0.474 points or 0.69 percent to 68.545 points on volume of 20.9 million shares worth $8.8 million.
Shenzhen's B index edged down 0.04 points or 0.02 percent to 155.48 points on turnover of HK$88.79 million, compared with Thursday's HK$52.34 million.
China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji called for measures to provide greater risk control on the financial markets, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday.

The newspaper also reported China's National People's Congress, or parliament, had decided to make securities-related fraud a crime rather than an irregularity in a draft amendment to the Criminal Law.
Brokers said the news helped cool the market's prevailing speculative mood, and this saw investors overcome by caution. They sold, but follow-up buying was thin.

"The recent over-speculative mood on the domestic A share market made investors concerned about measures the government might take to cool things down, and today's news is regarded as a sign," one broker based on the Shanghai market said.
"A correction is needed, with the index rising as it has over the past 10 days," another broker said.
Brokers based in Shenzhen said investors had little interest in buying with the approach of the weekend.
"Besides, many companies have yet to publish their annual results," one broker said.
Only 38 of China's 530 listed firms have issued their 1996 results with half of the reporting season already passed and the April 30 deadline approaching, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.
Of 43 firms with B shares listed in Shenzhen, only Fangda has issued its 1996 annual report, a spokesman for the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said.
In Shanghai, only one of 43 B share companies, Shanghai Hero Co Ltd, has issued its 1996 annual report.
Shanghai's A share index was slightly down, losing 1.302 points or 0.12 percent to 1,127.041 points on volume of 770.7 million shares worth 7.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index inched up 2.11 points or 0.07 percent to 2,863.069 points.

Shenzhen's A share index dipped 0.76 points or 0.19 percent to 395.32 on volume of 7.14 billion yuan on heavy profit-taking in a range of counters that appeared overvalued after recent sharp rises, brokers said.
Analysts said they expected the wary sentiment to extend into next week.
